# Legato

> A fast, open-source computer-use agent for any model (Apache-2.0). It uses a computer (clicks, types, reads the screen) with any OpenAI-compatible vision model: Qwen, Claude, GPT, Gemini, through OpenRouter, the maker's API, or a local server (vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio). Four ways in, one agent: the Mac app, `legato run` in a terminal, an MCP server for coding agents, and the Python package. It waits for the screen instead of sleeping and bounds every model call. PyPI name `legatolabs`, import name `legato`.

## Set up Legato for your user

Follow https://legato.computer/setup.md (the steps for coding agents). In short:

1. Install: `uv tool install legatolabs`, `pipx install legatolabs`, or `python3 -m pip install --user legatolabs`. There is no `pip install legato`.
2. `legato setup --json` prints what is missing. A key already in the environment (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) is used; otherwise ask the user for one and pass it on stdin: `printf '%s' "$KEY" | legato setup --yes --provider openrouter --api-key -`. Never invent a key. `--provider local` for a model server on this machine (no key).
3. Add `--mcp claude` (or `codex`, `cursor`, `claude-desktop`, `all`) to give that coding agent Legato's MCP server; the user starts a new session to see the tools.
4. On macOS, if setup lists Accessibility or Screen Recording as missing, tell the user which app to switch on in System Settings → Privacy & Security (the app that runs you); you cannot do it yourself.
5. Check: `legato run "On Wikipedia, look up the Eiffel Tower and tell me how tall it is" --json` gives `done: true` and an `answer`.

## Use it

- Terminal: `legato run "TASK"` (add `--json` for one JSON object with `status`, `done`, `answer`, `error`, `actions`, `wall_s`; `--timeout S` to cap it). Where: the saved desktop; on a Mac by default one app's window in the background (the app the task names, else the browser; `--app NAME` to choose), `--screen` for the whole screen, `--sandbox docker` for a desktop container, `--sandbox e2b` for a cloud desktop (`legatolabs[e2b]`, `E2B_API_KEY`).
- Python: `legato.run("TASK", timeout_s=None, cancel=None)` returns a RunResult (`status`: done, failed, max_steps, timeout, cancelled, stopped or error; `done`, `answer`, `error`, `usage`, `report()`); model and desktop errors come back as status `error`, not exceptions. Each part by hand: `agent = legato.Harness(model=..., base_url=..., api_key=...)`; `agent.run(task, desktop, max_steps=40)`. `legato.Harness()` with no model uses the saved one.
- Desktops in Python: `legato.local(background="Safari")` (macOS, one app's window, the person keeps using the Mac), `legato.local()` (this screen; moves the real mouse), `legato.providers.docker(w, h)` (returns `(stop, env)`), `legato.attach(Sandbox.create())` (E2B), `legato.attach(shell=fn_running_a_command_returning_stdout)` (any Linux sandbox with X, python3, xdotool, scrot), `legato.attach(screenshot=fn_returning_png_bytes, execute=fn_taking_legato_Action)` (anything else).
- MCP server (`legato mcp`, the saved desktop; or `--sandbox docker`, `--local`, `--sandbox file.py:function`). Tools: `desktop_open` (optional `url` or `app` to start first), `desktop_act` (returns the settled screenshot; no extra screenshot needed), `desktop_screenshot`, `desktop_shell` (a shell command on the desktop's computer), `desktop_run_task` (hand a whole task to Legato's own agent with the saved model; returns the answer), `desktop_close`. Apps on the host are at `http://host.docker.internal:PORT` inside the Docker desktop.
- Tools beside the screen: `legato.Harness(..., tools=[legato.tools.bash(env)])`; `legato.Tool(name, description, json_schema, handler)` wraps your own function.
- Coordinates: Claude models use pixels automatically; other models a 0-1000 grid. Set `coords=` for a model you have not checked. Raise `max_tokens` if `result.report()` shows cut-off turns.
- If anything fails: `legato doctor --json` reports what is installed and set up, with the fix for each.
